clip negatives to zero; lower on all 5 folds but only by 0.003 MW - GRU almost never predicts negative, so this is effectively a no-op

shrink far horizon (>12h) by 0.85, near horizon untouched; mean -0.13 MW but only F1/F5 improve while F2/F3/F4 worsen - direction is period-dependent, not established

replace far horizon (>24h) with fixed per-turbine metric-optimal constant fitted on raw fold_train (~290 kW); mean -0.11 MW but same split as 004 - F1/F5 better, F2/F3/F4 worse. Tail level is period-dependent, not a lever
anchor near horizon on last observed hour, decayed by per-fold rho(h) from FFT autocorr; fixes a real 47 kW under-anchoring at h=0 but only -0.05 MW and mixed folds; 15x slower (471s)
pooled farm-wide GRU (hidden 96, stride 6, per-turbine scalers) refit on all 5 folds into .cache/ckpt_007/{fold}; best inner-val at epoch 1-2 on every fold

score the pooled farm-wide GRU from ckpt_007; WORSE by 2.03 MW, F4 +5.8 and F3 +3.4; models stopped at epoch 1-2 because the trailing inner-val block measures period shift not generalization, so this tests the stopping rule as much as pooling
pooled retrain with one farm-wide scaler (fixes 207 kW cross-turbine level blowup) + interleaved 4-in-32-day holdout + lr 3e-4; into .cache/ckpt_009/{fold}; trains 3-5 epochs now vs 1-2 before

score pooled model from ckpt_009 (farm-wide scaler + interleaved holdout); 44.534 vs 46.235 for ckpt_007 so the scaler fix recovered 1.70 MW; still +0.33 vs seed but F1 -1.85 and F5 -1.96 while F4 +4.14 - large decorrelated errors vs the seed

ensemble seed per-turbine + pooled ckpt_009 at equal weight (members correlate only 0.64-0.67), retaining 006 anchoring; 44.060 best so far, beats the mean of its two members (44.369) on 4 of 5 folds - real variance reduction, but capped by the weaker member

pooled retrain with PER-COLUMN standardization (ColumnScaler) into .cache/ckpt_012/{fold}; under the seed scalar scaler Wspd carried 0.01% of post-scaling variance vs 78% for Patv; losses now ~0.7 not ~4.9 and inner-val decreases before rising. Code base recombines 009 pooled training with sampler parent 004

score pooled model with per-column standardization; WORSE by 1.23 MW vs same model with the seed scalar scaler (010), 4 of 5 folds worse, despite better-conditioned training - giving 9 nuisance channels equal weight dilutes the Patv signal that actually carries the forecast

three-member ensemble adding the per-column pooled model; 44.196 vs 44.060 for two members - diversity gain grew (0.64 MW below member average vs 0.31) but the weak member's bias outweighed it. Ensemble needs a better member, not just a different one

per-turbine GRU refit at hidden=96 (seed uses 48) under the improved 40/8/0.9 schedule into .cache/ckpt_015/{fold}; 670 jobs sharded 20-way (per-turbine seeding makes shards independent); seed notes recorded hidden 128 at 44.745 vs 45.136 but only under the OFFICIAL schedule
unmatched paren from a botched MEMBERS splice - evaluator rejected at import; logged rather than silently re-run since the scorer did execute

per-turbine hidden=96 refit scored alone; 44.025 best single model so far, but vs its exact comparator 006 (hidden=48, same anchoring) only -0.13 MW with 2 folds better and 3 worse - capacity gain is real but far smaller than the seed notes suggested because the improved schedule already captured most of it

three-member ensemble seed(48) + per-turbine hidden96 + pooled, equal weights; 43.936 new best, 4 of 5 folds below the seed (only F4 worse), 0.32 MW below its own member average (44.254) - the ensembling gain reappears now that all members are comparable

NameError _CACHES: my delete-until-next-def splice also removed the module-level cache block that sat between _anchors() and _resolve_path(); logged rather than silently re-run since the scorer executed

remove the 006 anchoring from the three-member ensemble; 43.917 new best, marginally better than 018 (43.936) with 108 fewer lines and 190s faster - simplification win, anchoring was never paying for itself

direct multi-horizon ridge fitted per fold inside forecast() (no retrain budget); 45.278 alone in 22.6s vs 935s for the GRU ensemble; fold profile is anti-correlated with the GRUs - better on F2 by 1.92 but worse on F1/F4 by ~2.9

four-member ensemble: 3 GRUs + per-horizon ridge at equal weight; 43.834 new best, 0.68 MW below its member average (44.510) - largest diversity gain yet, and the gain lands on F2 (-1.01) exactly where the ridge was anti-correlated with the GRUs

ridge + cubic wind terms + turbine climatology + 14d/7d farm lags; WORSE by 1.21 MW vs the 9-feature ridge (021), 4 of 5 folds worse - second independent case (after 013) of extra channels diluting the Patv signal on this task

Patv-only ridge, 7 features, no wind; 45.747 - WORSE than the 9-feature ridge with two wind columns (45.278) by 0.47. So the 023 lesson was not 'fewer features always win': 9 features beats both 7 and 15, there is an optimum

combine the 4-member ensemble by half mean half median to match the metric's 0.5*(RMSE+MAE) structure; 43.835 vs 43.834 for the plain mean - no effect, since with 4 members the median IS the mean of the middle two. Keep the simpler mean

gradient-boosted member on the ridge features + time-of-day, 14 anchor horizons interpolated; 45.153 alone in 33s, beats the ridge (45.278). Needed denser origins first: phase-locked origins gave only ~80 effective samples (134 turbines per origin are 0.92 correlated) and the horizon profile jumped 128->321->203 kW

five-member ensemble adding the GBM at equal weight; 43.984 vs 43.834 for four members - diversity gain held (0.66 below member average) but the member average rose from 44.51 to 44.64 and swamped it. Same saturation as 014

four slots with ridge and GBM sharing the statistical slot at 0.125 each; 43.920 vs 43.834 for the ridge alone in that slot - averaging the two statistical models did not beat the better-placed single one. NOTE eval_seconds not comparable across runs (background contention)

smooth ridge coefficients along the horizon axis (13-step moving average, intercept left unsmoothed); 45.138 vs 45.278 and lower on ALL FIVE folds - 2592 coefficients were being fitted from ~87 effective origins, so neighbouring horizons differed mostly by estimation noise
four-member ensemble with the horizon-smoothed ridge; 43.825 new best, lower on all 5 folds vs 022 (43.834) - the ridge's 0.14 MW gain arrives diluted by its 0.25 weight, which is the expected size

ridge with per-turbine intercepts (fitted offsets std 37.5 kW, matching the 38.0 kW persistent spread measured in raw data); 45.177 vs 45.138 - neutral-to-slightly-worse, 2 folds better 3 worse. The trailing-mean features already encode the persistent level

same linear design fitted by least absolute deviations (targets the conditional median, metric-aligned with the MAE half); 46.705 vs 45.138 for the L2 fit, fold_std 6.59. F5 much better (-4.03) and the other four much worse - textbook period-specific artefact, F5 being the low-wind fold where a median forecast wins

drop the redundant seed GRU (correlates 0.93-0.94 with the hidden=96 refit vs 0.56-0.79 for every other pair), leaving 3 distinct members; 43.841 vs 43.825 - neutral, 3 folds better 2 worse. Double-weighting the strongest family was not actually hurting, so the redundancy argument does not hold here

farm-decomposition forecaster: fit the farm-average series directly, add each turbine's permanent offset, carry its current deviation forward at the deviation's own measured autocorrelation; 45.148, tied with the smoothed ridge (45.138) but different fold profile (F2 -0.56, F4 +0.63). Internal estimates match raw-data measurements (offset std 38-39 kW, rho_dev 0.41/0.13/0.05)

three statistical members (ridge + GBM + farm decomposition) averaged, no checkpoints at all; 44.616 vs 45.138/45.148/45.153 individually - 0.53 MW below the best member and below the member average. Fitted entirely at scoring time in 53s, within 0.41 MW of the 134-GRU seed

ensemble with the averaged statistical trio in the fourth slot; 43.854 vs 43.825 with the ridge alone there - a STRONGER slot member made the ensemble slightly worse. Pre-averaging the three removed the very between-member variance the ensemble was cancelling, so member quality and member diversity trade off

analog forecaster: match the farm's last 24h against same-phase days in the fold's history, average what followed; 46.294 - too weak for the slot (library is only 87-207 days, cannot match extreme origins) but very decorrelated, producing the best F3 of any member at 38.84

feed the GRUs a 432-step prefix at inference instead of the 144 they trained on; 44.128 vs 43.825 - worse by 0.30, mostly F1 (+0.41) and F4 (+1.17). The extra context is a train/test mismatch and the hidden state settles somewhere the projection was not fitted for

ridge fitted on origins every 4h instead of one per day, with origin-phase sin/cos so each horizon can still recover the diurnal cycle (sin(t+h) expands linearly in sin t, cos t); 44.653 vs 45.138, better on 4 of 5 folds (F4 -1.75, F5 -1.06). Same effective-sample-size fix that rescued the GBM

ensemble with the much better dense-origin ridge (44.653 vs 45.138 solo); 43.947 vs 43.825 - the ensemble got WORSE. Verified mechanism: the dense ridge correlates 0.783 with the GRU consensus vs 0.639 for the sparse one, so it gained 0.485 in accuracy and lost 0.144 in decorrelation, which the slot is actually paying for

put the analog (worse solo 46.294 but least correlated, rho 0.553) in the slot instead of the ridge, as the decorrelation criterion predicted; 43.980 vs 43.825 - PREDICTION FAILED. Best F3 of any ensemble (38.41) but F2 much worse. Prediction-correlation is not error-correlation: the analog's independence comes largely from BIAS (it cannot match extreme origins), and bias adds under averaging rather than cancelling

farm-decomposition model in the fourth slot instead of the ridge; 43.764 NEW BEST, F1 -0.22 and F2 -0.25 vs 030. Falsifies the decorrelation criterion a second time - it ranked farm (rho 0.707, cost 652) well below ridge (rho 0.639, cost 601) and the opposite held

GBM in the fourth slot - the last untested candidate; 44.071, worst of the five. Final slot table: farm 43.764, ridge 43.825, trio 43.854, dense ridge 43.947, analog 43.980, gbm 44.071. Neither solo score nor prediction-correlation orders this list (analog rho 0.553 ranks 5th, farm rho 0.707 ranks 1st) - the spread is 0.31 MW, inside noise

dense-origin farm model in the slot (24x the training rows); 43.937 vs 43.764 for the sparse version - WORSE. Second clean within-family A/B: sparse ridge 43.825 vs dense ridge 43.947, sparse farm 43.764 vs dense farm 43.937. Within a member family the leaner, noisier fit is the better ensemble member even though it is the worse forecaster

four slots for four model classes (per-turbine GRU + pooled GRU + ridge + farm), dropping the duplicate seed GRU; 43.915 vs 43.764 - worse overall despite the best F2 of any ensemble (46.36 vs 47.06), lost on F4 (+0.91). Spending a slot on a second statistical class costs more than the near-duplicate GRU it replaced

blend toward climatology for turbines whose input window is >50% abnormal (16.9% of turbine-windows, 30.6% on F5); 43.891 vs 43.764 - worse, and the loss is entirely F5 (+0.594) where the trigger rate is highest, every other fold within 0.02. Curtailment PERSISTS: a turbine idle for the last day tends to stay idle, so the models' near-zero forecast was right and climatology over-predicts

horizon-dependent family weights: statistical share doubled from 0.25 to 0.50 past 24h where the GRU tail is flat to 1.1 kW; 43.971 vs 43.764 - worse on 4 of 5 folds. The GRU's flat tail beats a directly-fitted per-horizon climatology, consistent with 005 - a climatology fitted on the training period does not transfer to the validation period, while the sequence models' tail does

mirror of 047 - statistical share HALVED past 24h instead of doubled; 43.711 NEW BEST, better on 4 of 5 folds vs 042 (43.764). Two-sided test settles it: the far horizon wants more sequence model, and a per-horizon climatology fitted on the training period does not transfer to the validation period

statistical members removed entirely from the far horizon (share ramps 0.25 -> 0 between 12h and 24h); 43.692 NEW BEST, better on 4 of 5 folds vs 048. Endpoint of the direction 047/048 established: past 24h every member emits a level not a forecast, and the GRUs' level transfers across periods while a fitted climatology does not

re-run the slot contest under near-horizon-only weighting: ridge instead of farm; 43.746 vs 43.692 - farm still wins the slot, so the 042 ranking carries over and is not an artefact of the uniform weighting it was measured under

replace 049's hand-picked 12h-24h ramp with a parameter-free schedule proportional to the measured farm autocorrelation; 43.821 vs 43.692 - WORSE. It ramps out too fast (stat share 0.078 by 6h vs 0.25), so the statistical member's value is not purely persistence: its per-horizon intercepts carry diurnal climatology useful where rho is already low. NOTE this means 049's schedule is hand-picked and may be partly fitted to this split

tilt the GRU family by horizon - pooled member's share rises to 0.667 past 24h since its tail level came from 134x more windows; 43.809 vs 43.692 - worse overall, but best F1 (45.54) and best F5 (37.41) of any ensemble while losing F2 +0.42 and F4 +0.65. The pooled model's tail is better in some periods and worse in others, matching its solo per-fold instability

farm and ridge share the near-horizon slot at 0.125 each; 43.717 vs 43.692 - neutral to slightly worse, so 028's result was not an artefact of the uniform weighting it was measured under. Pre-averaging two members removes variance the ensemble would otherwise cancel, near horizon included

drop the duplicate seed GRU under the tail-handover weighting (2 GRUs at 0.375 + farm 0.25); 43.696 vs 43.692 - a tie, with one fewer checkpoint set needed. Fold signature matches 052: F1 -0.34 and F5 -0.37 better, F4 +0.64 worse, the recurring trade-off whenever the pooled model's tail share rises

re-test the dense-origin farm fit with the statistical member confined to the near horizon; 43.881 vs 43.692 - still worse, so the 040/044 finding was NOT specific to the tail. A better-fitted statistical member homogenises toward the GRUs in the near horizon too, and the original wording of that conclusion stands

add 10-min and 30-min trailing means to the near-horizon member, on the theory that short lags pay once the member only speaks inside 24h; 43.740 vs 43.692 - worse. Even confined to where persistence is strongest, extra features cost more than they add, matching 013/023/024

admit the weaker pooled GRU (ckpt_012, 45.76 solo) to the TAIL ONLY, taking the share the statistical member vacates; 43.764 vs 43.692 - worse. F2 better (-0.26) but F1/F4/F5 worse. Averaging two pooled level estimates does not beat one, so the tail level is not limited by estimation noise in the level itself

deviation-term ablation crashed: farm_hat is (1,288) not (288,), so my broadcast_to((capacity,output_len)) failed. Process error too - I put the verification snippet inside the background command, so its failure never reached me before scoring

ablate the farm member's transient-deviation term, leaving farm level + per-turbine constant; 43.696 vs 43.692 - a tie on every fold (max fold difference 0.011). The term carries a 153 kW spread but decorrelates to 0.13 by 6h, and the GRUs already cover that region. Simplification win: drops the term and its rho_dev estimation

ablate the per-turbine offsets too, leaving one farm trajectory broadcast to all 134 turbines (verified: across-turbine spread 39.1 -> 0.0 kW); 43.708 vs 43.696 - costs 0.012, so offsets are nearly free but not quite. 059 is the sweet spot: deviation term out, offsets in

INTENDED as a three-GRU control but the weights do not sum to 1: _family_weight scales GRUs up in the tail to absorb the statistical member's vacated share, so with no statistical member the total reaches 1.333 past 24h and the tail is inflated 33%. Scored 45.627; this measures an inflated-tail program, NOT the control. The forecast mean was 575.9 vs ~486 for 049 and I should have caught it in verification

correctly normalised three-GRU control (weights verified 1.000 at every horizon); 43.9166 - EXACTLY reproduces 020 to 11 decimals, which was the same three members before the ridge was added, so the pipeline is deterministic and the weighting is right. The statistical member is therefore worth 43.917-43.692 = 0.224 MW, not the 1.93 that 061's inflated tail suggested

raise the statistical member's near-horizon share from 0.25 to 0.35 (weights verified 1.000 at every horizon); 43.642 NEW BEST, F2 -0.31 and F1 -0.10, F4 +0.13. The 0.25 was inherited from when there were simply four members and was never a considered choice

second step on the near-horizon share, 0.35 -> 0.45; 43.615 NEW BEST but the gain halves (0.050 then 0.027), so this is a plateau not a slope. F1 -0.08 and F2 -0.27, F4 +0.15. STOPPING on this knob as pre-committed - a third point would be sweeping

re-test 059's deviation-term ablation at the 0.45 share; 43.628 vs 43.615 - costs 0.013 now versus 0.0035 at share 0.25, so the term earns a little more when the member speaks louder but is still nearly free. 064 stays nominally best, 065 is the simpler near-tie

share the 0.45 near-horizon slot between farm and ridge; 43.647 vs 43.615 - third loss for slot-sharing after 028 (uniform, 43.920) and 053 (0.25 share, 43.717), this time at the largest slot and therefore its best chance. Settled: pre-averaging two members always removes more between-member variance than it gains

drop the duplicate seed GRU at the 0.45 share (2 GRUs at 0.275 each + farm 0.45); 43.621 vs 43.615 - a tie for the third time (33: 43.841 vs 43.825; 054: 43.696 vs 43.692), now with one fewer checkpoint set. F1 -0.31 and F5 -0.32 better, F4 +0.56 worse - the same trade-off as always

GBM in the near-horizon slot at 0.45, completing the slot table; 44.054 vs 43.615 - still last, as it was at uniform weights (44.071). The slot ranking farm > ridge > ... > GBM is stable across both weightings and both slot sizes

split the statistical share by horizon - analogue owns h<6h, farm owns 6-24h, GRUs own past 24h (weights verified 1.000 throughout); 43.740 vs 43.615 - worse. Second-best F3 of any ensemble (38.878) but the analogue's library-mean bias costs more elsewhere even confined to the first hours

combine both simplifications - drop the duplicate seed GRU AND ablate the deviation term; 43.633 vs 43.615, cost 0.018 where the two individual costs were 0.006 and 0.013, so they are almost exactly additive. Buys 2 checkpoint sets instead of 3 and a statistical member that is just a farm trajectory plus a per-machine constant

remove the per-turbine offsets too - statistical member is now one farm trajectory broadcast to all 134 turbines; 43.662 vs 43.633, costing 0.029 (was 0.012 at the 0.25 share, so it scales with how loudly the member speaks). Simplicity frontier: 064 43.615 full / 070 43.633 two-thirds / 071 43.662 none

remove the pooled GRU to price it; 43.681 vs 43.615 - worth only 0.066 MW net, far less than its diversity (correlates 0.64-0.70 with the per-turbine models vs 0.93 between them) suggests. F4 -0.64 and F2 -0.32 better without it, F1 +0.76 and F5 +0.52 worse; fold_std falls to 4.171, the most balanced of any ensemble

minimal ensemble - one GRU (hidden=96 refit) plus the farm member; 43.664 vs 43.615 for three checkpoint sets, so the two extra GRUs are worth 0.049 MW combined. Also beats 072's two-per-turbine-GRU variant (43.681). fold_std 4.201. A program needing ONE checkpoint set matches one needing three

simplest program worth keeping: one GRU (hidden=96) + farm trajectory + per-turbine offsets, 0.45 of the near horizon, none of the tail; 43.679 vs 43.615 - costs 0.064 for a third of the trained artefacts and no autocorrelation machinery. Landed exactly on the 43.68 prediction

lightly smooth the farm member's per-horizon intercept (5 steps = 50 min); 43.6147 vs 43.6151 - a tie, identical on every fold. Roughness halved (6.39 -> 3.86 kW/step) while the diurnal range held at 197 kW, so the 029 worry about flattening the cycle was avoidable, but the noise it removed was not costing anything

raise the farm fit's penalty from 1% to 10% of the diagonal, on the argument that 87 origins x 7 features needs more shrinkage than the pooled ridge's 11k rows; 43.902 vs 43.615 - much worse. Unlike the ridge's horizon-smoothing (029, helped on all 5 folds), this fit's coefficients carry signal and shrinking them costs

INTENDED as the mirror of 076 but was a no-op: I assumed the farm fit inherited RIDGE_ALPHA=1e-2, but that value came from 023 which was discarded, and the live lineage had 1e-3 all along. Setting FARM_ALPHA=1e-3 therefore changed nothing and reproduced 064 to 15 decimals (mean|beta| 104.1336 both). So the knob is only known at 1e-1 (43.902, worse) and 1e-3 (43.615)

farm-fit penalty lowered to 1e-4 (the genuine mirror of 076); 43.606 NEW BEST, 3 folds better. Knob now characterised at 1e-4 43.606 / 1e-3 43.615 / 1e-1 43.902 - monotone, lighter is better, consistent with the farm target being the average of 134 turbines and so ~sqrt(134) cleaner than any single series. Stopping here as the 1e-3 to 1e-4 gain is only 0.009

halve the farm fit's horizon smoothing (13 -> 7 steps), by analogy with 078's lighter penalty; 43.611 vs 43.606 - slightly worse. The two shrinkage axes disagree: the farm fit wants a tenth the ridge's PENALTY but the same SMOOTHING width, so the analogy from 078 does not transfer

drop the farm member's 7-day lag; 43.567 NEW BEST, 3 folds better, and it does three things at once - removes a feature that only carried a level the intercept already supplies, and frees RIDGE_HISTORY from 1008 to 144 so each fold gains ~6 origins (87 -> 93 on F1)

drop the 24h lag as well: SINGULAR MATRIX. CORRECTED DIAGNOSIS (see 082): not collinearity but RIDGE_HISTORY=36 yielding zero origins, since origins are phase-filtered to =143 mod 144 and 35 mod 144 = 35

same singular matrix as 081 despite raising the penalty - because my 081 diagnosis was WRONG. It is not collinearity: origins start at RIDGE_HISTORY-1 and are then filtered to the 23:50 phase (=143 mod 144), so RIDGE_HISTORY=36 gives 35 mod 144 = 35 and the filter removes EVERY origin. 1008 and 144 are multiples of 144 and work; 36 is not

drop the farm member's 24h lag with origins held fixed at 93; 43.461 NEW BEST, 3 folds better including F4 -0.36 and F1 -0.24. Second confirmation that long trailing means carry only a LEVEL the per-horizon intercept already supplies - 7d helped (080), 24h helps more, and this one is clean of the origin-count confound

drop the 6h lag as well; 43.620 vs 43.461 - WORSE, so the removal run stops. Optimal farm lag set is (1h, 3h, 6h), which is exactly the span where Patv autocorrelation is still meaningful (0.77 / 0.52 / 0.28) before it decays to a level the intercept supplies

remove the farm member's 6h WIND lag; 43.870 vs 43.461 - much worse, 0.409. Asymmetry worth noting: removing the 6h POWER lag cost 0.159 but the 6h WIND lag costs 0.409, so wind history carries lead information that power history does not - wind causes power, so it leads it

add a 3h wind lag so wind matches power's resolution; 43.4545 NEW BEST, 3 folds better. Confirms 085's asymmetry - wind is the more informative channel and rewards resolution, which also narrows the old 013/023 conclusion: ELABORATE wind features lose, plain trailing wind means are the most valuable columns here

raise the statistical share to 0.55 now that the member has materially improved (080/083/086/078 worth ~0.15 MW to it); 43.412 NEW BEST, F1 -0.12 and F2 -0.24. Re-testing after the premises changed, not sweeping - the share stops at 0.55

score the improved statistical member ALONE across the full horizon; 44.362 vs 45.148 when built (034) - it improved 0.786 MW on its own account via the lag surgery and lighter penalty. Now only 0.155 MW behind the 134-model GRU seed baseline (44.207), fitted from scratch per fold in ~1s. This justifies the 0.55 share: the member is genuinely comparable to the GRUs (44.03-44.53)

deviation-term ablation at the current best (share 0.55, improved member); 43.431 vs 43.412 - costs 0.019, up from 0.0035 at share 0.25 and 0.013 at 0.45. The cost tracks the share almost linearly, and the term remains cheap to remove even now the member is strong

minimal program re-run with the improved member: ONE GRU + farm at 0.55; 43.458 vs 43.412 for three GRUs - costs 0.046, and fold_std 4.036 is the most balanced of the run. With the member now within 0.16 MW of the whole seed baseline, two of the three checkpoint sets are close to redundant

smallest justifiable program: one GRU + a six-feature fold-fitted ridge with per-turbine offsets; 43.479 vs 43.412 - costs 0.067, against a predicted 0.065. One training run instead of three, no autocorrelation machinery, ~37s to score

extend the handover to 18h-36h now the member is strong; 43.395 NEW BEST, F1 -0.13 and F2 -0.28 though F3/F5 worse. Reverses 047, which found extending the OLD member into the tail cost 0.21 MW - that member scored 45.148 at a 0.25 share, this one scores 44.362 at 0.55. Stopping on this knob; the fold split (2 better, 3 worse) says the 0.017 is near noise

minimal program with 092's longer handover; 43.448 vs 43.479 for the shorter one, and only 0.053 behind the best three-GRU program. fold_std 3.949 is the LOWEST of the run - the most period-consistent forecaster built here, on one checkpoint set

re-price the pooled GRU against the improved member; 43.445 vs 43.395 - still costs 0.050, down from 0.066 at 072, so the substitution with the farm member is partial not complete. But fold_std falls 4.107 -> 3.927, the lowest of the run: removing it trades 0.05 of mean for markedly better period consistency

add a 10-minute WIND lag; 43.305 NEW BEST by 0.090, with F3 -0.47, F1 -0.23, F5 -0.20. Third confirmation that wind leads power: 056 lost 0.048 adding short POWER lags, but the same resolution on WIND gains 0.090 - a power reading says where the turbine is, a wind reading says where it is about to be
add a 30-minute wind lag to fill the ladder; 43.345 vs 43.305 - worse by 0.040, so the wind ladder is complete at four rungs (10min, 1h, 3h, 6h). Stopping the direction as pre-committed

final recommended program: ONE checkpoint set + a seven-feature fold-fitted ridge with per-turbine offsets; 43.362 vs 43.305 for the three-GRU best - only 0.057 behind on a third of the trained artefacts, 38s to score. fold_std 4.157

re-test a 10-minute POWER lag in the redesigned member; 43.350 vs 43.305 - still worse, so 056's verdict survives the member being rebuilt around it. Short wind lags pay (+0.090), short power lags do not (-0.045), in two quite different designs. F1 improved 0.19 but F3 lost 0.32

wind enters as mean(v^3) instead of mean(v), same feature count; 43.282 NEW BEST, 4 of 5 folds better (F4 -0.35, F2 -0.19). Vindicates the physics that 023 got wrong: that experiment ADDED v/v^2/v^3 over overlapping windows and lost 1.21 MW to collinearity, this REPLACES and gains. Power goes as v^3, and mean(v^3) differs from (mean v)^3 by the within-window gustiness
carry cubic wind into the one-checkpoint program; 43.355 vs 43.362 - a small gain, and it stays 0.072 behind the three-checkpoint best (43.282) on a third of the artefacts

average-of-cubes crashed: NoneType.reshape - the predict path calls _farm_design without the new farm_cube argument, since my edit targeted an 'Xf = ...' form that exists in other lineages but not this one. Third time I have put the verification inside the background command so its failure never reached me before scoring

average per-turbine cubes instead of cubing the farm average; 43.301 vs 43.282 - slightly WORSE despite a real 5.3% Jensen gap between the two quantities. The physics picks the right quantity in principle, but the cross-turbine wind spread behaves more like noise than signal here, and the cube-of-average is the smoother regressor
